_howToEdit: A rotation is display and damage in one object, so editing it can never desync the two.
groups[].steps[] = { icon, action, char, note, flags, hits }
icon   -> icons/<icon>.png. Missing files fall back to a letter tile, so add art any time.
hits   -> the ability instances this press actually fires, as exact labels from
ref/proj-<char>.json. A string, or { ability, times }. Omit for a switch or a wait.
raw    -> a fixed number instead (echo-skill damage, which the reference data lacks).
A group with count:false is shown but excluded from the total (loop repeats, traversal).
To add a character: put them in characters.json, run tools/refresh-ref.sh, then use their
labels here. To try a variant, copy a rotation, change its id, and edit the steps.

BUFF WINDOWS live on the ROTATION, not on the buff: rotations[].windows maps a buff id to [fromStep, untilStep]. Both inclusive, 1-based, and they use the SAME step number printed on the icon tile — read it off the page and type it in. null on either end means open. Step numbers are per-rotation and the same buff appears in rotations of different lengths, which is why this cannot live on the buff: a fromStep of 14 that is correct for the 31-step team loop cuts the 14-step solo loop in half. A buff with no window behaves exactly as before windows existed. A window naming a buff the rotation does not list, or an inverted/out-of-range window, is a loud validate.mjs failure. The page draws every buff as a bar under the rotation: gold = windowed, grey = no window, i.e. an assumption rather than a measurement.

notes.t: STEP ZERO — check Aemeath's Resonance Mode
notes.b: In the team-building menu, under her portrait, there is a toggle: Tune Rupture or Fusion Burst. It must say Fusion Burst. Never switch modes mid-fight — it resets Aemeath's 60% Crit DMG and her 25% Finale amplification.

notes.t: The star budget has ZERO slack
notes.b: Overdrive after an Intro = +2. Duet #1 = +3. Duet #2 = +4. Those are the only three sources in her kit. Only the Finale spends them. If one Duet fails to fire you finish at 3/4 and the Finale can never light up that rotation.

notes.t: The single most common mistake — Stage 4 only
notes.b:
Seraphic Duet needs two things at once: you are in Seraphic Duo, and you have at least 100 in the bar. Seraphic Duo opens on Basic Attack Stage 4 only and lasts 5s. The Sync Strike window is wider — stages 2, 3 or 4 — and stages 2 and 3 can never give you a star. A full bar with two stars is exactly what that looks like.
Shortcut: Dodge Counter → Normal Attack casts Stage 4 directly.

notes.t: The 6-second rule on Suisui — this is the whole trick
notes.b: Suisui's biggest buff is a two-hop chain. She Outros out, and about 6 seconds later her first Plume Step lands. Only then does the character on field gain "your Outro hands Undulating Mist to the next character in". So Verina must hold the field to at least the 6-second mark. Swap early and the chain never forms.

notes.t: What Aemeath actually gets from Suisui at S0
notes.b: The headline +50% ATK needs a character who consumes Negative Status stacks. Aemeath inflicts without consuming, so at S0 it does not reach her — Suisui S1 is the fix. What does land: +3 to the Fusion Burst max stack limit (10 → 13), worth about 18% of the whole rotation, plus 25% All DMG Amp, 25% team ATK, 20% from Firstlight's Herald and healing.

notes.t: If the loop feels like it's failing
notes.b: Her +18 Concerto and the team heal share a 25-second internal cooldown. A full team loop runs about 25.3 seconds, so the margin is a fraction of a second. Play faster than that and Suisui loses both on alternating cycles and will fail to Outro. Slow down rather than adding presses.

notes.t: The trick: cast a THIRD enhanced skill
notes.b: Overdrive without an Intro gives +1 Resonance Rate instead of +2, so two enhanced skills only reach 3 of 4. The fix is a third Seraphic Duet. There is no cast limit — the "2" people remember is Stardust Resonance, the damage buff, which stops enhancing after two casts. Overdrive (1) + three Duets (3) = 4/4.

Stand out of combat ~4 seconds without heavy-attacking and she enters Instant Response - Brilliance. A Heavy Charged II there grants 100 Synchronization, even outside Unbound. The heavy drops the state, so wait ~4s and repeat: you enter the fight at 200/200. This is what your S1 node is actually for.

notes.t: No Suisui means no stack-cap raise
notes.b: Fusion Burst runs at 10 stacks solo, not 13, because the +3 comes from Suisui's Ceaseless Landscape. That alone is most of the gap between these two numbers.

notes.t: The real solo constraint is energy, not stars
notes.b: Overdrive costs Resonance Energy and there is no Outro or off-field generation feeding you. Energy does carry between fights in the open world.

notes.b: Her passive Blazing Valor only fires after she has been out of combat for more than 4 seconds, and it is what gives her the first Majesty stack. Stand still ~5s and watch for the Majesty pip. It does not re-trigger mid-fight.

notes.t: Why the party order is fixed
notes.b: Mortefi's Outro (38% Heavy Attack Deepen, 14s) has to land on Augusta, so he is always the last hop. Augusta's Outro has to land on someone who Outros onward within 14s — that hand-off pays her a Majesty stack. So Baizhi sits in the middle.

notes.t: Two Ultimates on one button — TAP vs HOLD
notes.b: Tap for Sword of Eternal Oath (stage 1, costs energy, counts as Heavy Attack damage, +40% Ascendancy). Hold for Sublime is the Sun (stage 2, zero energy, 2 Majesty, stops time 7s). Tapping when you meant to hold wastes the cycle.

notes.t: Buffs freeze during the time stop
notes.b: Mortefi's 38% and Augusta's own buffs do not tick down during the 7s of Sworn Allegiance. That is why her backloaded finisher still lands fully buffed.

notes.t: ⚠️ These numbers are not trustworthy yet
